Build a historiograph (chronological citation network)

Source: R/historiograph.R
historiograph.Rd

historiograph() builds a Garfield-style historiograph (Garfield, 2004): the n most locally cited documents and the within-corpus citations they receive, each edge carrying the publication years of both ends so the network can be laid out chronologically. The citing document of an edge may be any document in the data, not only one of the n selected.

Usage

historiograph(
  data,
  n = 30,
  min_lcs = 1,
  references = "references",
  sep = ";",
  strip_quotes = TRUE,
  id = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per work, a references column (list-column or delimited string) whose values use the same identifiers as the works, and year. An id column is optional (see id). Optionally title, journal, doi, cited_by_count.

n

Integer. Number of top locally cited documents to include. Default 30.

min_lcs

Integer. Minimum local citation score for inclusion. Default 1.

references

Character. Name of the column containing cited references. Default "references".

sep

Character. Separator used to split the references column when it is a plain character column. Default ";".

strip_quotes

Logical. If TRUE (default), surrounding quote characters are removed from each reference.

id

Optional. Name of the column to use as the work identifier. If NULL (default), an existing id column is used when present, otherwise row numbers are used.

Value

A list of two data frames:

nodes

One row per included document (at most n, each with lcs >= min_lcs), with the local_citations() columns (id, lcs, gcs when available, year, and title, journal, doi when present), sorted by decreasing lcs.

edges

One row per distinct directed citation that points at an included document, with from (citing; any document in the data), to (cited), year_from and year_to (integer), sorted by year_from then year_to.

Both are empty (zero rows) when no document reaches min_lcs.

Details

The documents are ranked by local_citations(); n and min_lcs set how many are kept. It returns a list with a nodes and an edges data frame.

References

Garfield, E. (2004). Historiographic mapping of knowledge domains literature. Journal of Information Science, 30(2), 119–145. doi:10.1177/0165551504042802

Examples

data(biblio_data)
historiograph(biblio_data, n = 5)
#> $nodes
#>   id lcs gcs year                                         title
#> 1 W1   7  45 2018 Co-citation analysis of scientific literature
#> 2 W2   4  32 2019    Bibliographic coupling and research fronts
#> 3 W3   2  18 2020          Fractional counting in bibliometrics
#> 4 W5   1  12 2021      Community detection in citation networks
#>                   journal            doi
#> 1          Scientometrics 10.1000/test.1
#> 2 Journal of Informetrics 10.1000/test.2
#> 3          Scientometrics 10.1000/test.3
#> 4 Journal of Informetrics 10.1000/test.5
#> 
#> $edges
#>    from to year_from year_to
#> 1    W2 W1      2019    2018
#> 2    W4 W1      2019    2018
#> 3    W9 W1      2019    2018
#> 4    W4 W2      2019    2019
#> 5    W9 W2      2019    2019
#> 6    W3 W1      2020    2018
#> 7    W6 W1      2020    2018
#> 8    W6 W2      2020    2019
#> 9    W5 W1      2021    2018
#> 10  W10 W2      2021    2019
#> 11   W5 W3      2021    2020
#> 12  W10 W3      2021    2020
#> 13   W8 W1      2022    2018
#> 14   W8 W5      2022    2021
#>
